decisions.reason: The air quality sensor module is a dedicated, sunk-cost investment in the firm's announced sensor-expansion direction, so management will keep it and attribute any weak demand to temporary causes such as the chip shortage.
As the publicly announced replacement in the hardware-generation roadmap, the voltage module is central to the platform and would only leave if superseded by a newer version.
The MQTT proxy reinforces the software-binding strength the firm promotes and is cheap to maintain, so dropping it would undercut the firm's stated direction.
The CAN bus module fits the connectivity roadmap and its development cost is sunk, so management keeps it despite its lower visibility and blames weak sales on component supply problems.
The CO2 sensor module has a dedicated page and matches the sensor strategy, so continued commitment is expected even if a newer generation is in planning.
The touch panel is a visible ecosystem complement the firm has committed to, so it is likely retained, though as an accessory it is somewhat more exposed to being discontinued.
